title: Bekhorot 35
description: A Roman quaestor and some playing children blemish firstborns, why one who kicks a pursuing firstborn may slaughter it, blemishing a firstborn before it is born, and who is trusted to testify that a blemish was not caused on purpose.

a1.he: טִימֵּא טְהָרוֹת וָמֵת — לֹא קָנְסוּ בְּנוֹ אַחֲרָיו. מַאי טַעְמָא? הֶיזֵּק שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִיכָּר לָא שְׁמֵיהּ הֶיזֵּק, קְנָסָא דְּרַבָּנַן — לְדִידֵיהּ קְנַסוּ רַבָּנַן, לִבְרֵיהּ לָא קְנַסוּ רַבָּנַן.

a2.he: מַתְנִי׳ מַעֲשֶׂה בְּזָכָר שֶׁל רְחֵלִים זָקֵן, וּשְׂעָרוֹ מְדוּלְדָּל, וְרָאָהוּ קַסְטוֹר אֶחָד וְאָמַר: מָה טִיבוֹ שֶׁל זֶה? אָמְרוּ לוֹ: בְּכוֹר הוּא, וְאֵינוֹ נִשְׁחָט אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הָיָה בּוֹ מוּם. נָטַל (פיגום) [פִּיגְיוֹם] וְצָרַם אׇזְנוֹ, וּבָא מַעֲשֶׂה לִפְנֵי חֲכָמִים וְהִתִּירוּ, וְאַחַר שֶׁהִתִּירוּ הָלַךְ וְצֵירֵם בְּאׇזְנֵי בְכוֹרוֹת אֲחֵרִים וְאָסְרוּ.

a3.he: פַּעַם אַחַת הָיוּ תִּינוֹקוֹת מְשַׂחֲקִין בַּשָּׂדֶה, וְקָשְׁרוּ זַנְבֵי טְלָאִים זֶה בָּזֶה, וְנִפְסְקָה זְנָבוֹ שֶׁל אֶחָד מֵהֶם, וַהֲרֵי הוּא בְּכוֹר, וּבָא מַעֲשֶׂה לִפְנֵי חֲכָמִים וְהִתִּירוּ. רָאוּ שֶׁהִתִּירוּ, הָלְכוּ וְקָשְׁרוּ זַנְבוֹת בְּכוֹרוֹת אֲחֵרִים, וְאָסְרוּ. זֶה הַכְּלָל: כֹּל שֶׁהוּא לְדַעְתּוֹ — אָסוּר, שֶׁלֹּא לְדַעְתּוֹ — מוּתָּר.

a4.he: גְּמָ׳ פַּעַם אַחֶרֶת הָיָה כּוּ׳. וּצְרִיכָא, דְּאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן גּוֹי — דְּלָא אָתֵי לְמִיסְרַךְ, אֲבָל קָטָן דְּאָתֵי לְמִיסְרַךְ — אֵימָא לָא.

a5.he: וְאִי אַשְׁמוֹעִינַן קָטָן, מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא אָתֵי לְאִיחַלּוֹפֵי בְּגָדוֹל, אֲבָל גּוֹי דְּאָתֵי לְאִיחַלּוֹפֵי בְּגָדוֹל — אֵימָא לָא. צְרִיכָא.

a6.he: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר רַב קַטִּינָא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא דַּאֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ ״אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הָיָה בּוֹ מוּם״, אֲבָל אִם אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ ״אִם נַעֲשָׂה בּוֹ מוּם״ — כְּמַאן דַּאֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ ״זִיל עֲבֵיד בֵּיהּ מוּמָא״ דָּמֵי.

a7.he: אָמַר רָבָא: מִכְּדֵי מִמֵּילָא הוּא, מָה לִי ״הָיָה״, מָה לִי ״נַעֲשָׂה״? אֶלָּא ״נַעֲשָׂה״ נָמֵי מִמֵּילָא הוּא, וְלָא שְׁנָא.

a8.he: זֶה הַכְּלָל: כֹּל שֶׁהוּא לְדַעַת — אָסוּר. לְאֵיתוֹיֵי מַאי? לְאֵיתוֹיֵי גְּרָמָא.

a9.he: שֶׁלֹּא לְדַעַת — לְאֵיתוֹיֵי מֵסִיחַ לְפִי תוּמּוֹ.

a10.he: מַתְנִי׳ הָיָה בְּכוֹר רֹדְפוֹ, בְּעָטוֹ, וְעָשָׂה בּוֹ מוּם — הֲרֵי זֶה שׁוֹחֲטִין עָלָיו.

a11.he: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁבְּעָטוֹ בִּשְׁעַת רְדִיפָה, אֲבָל לְאַחַר רְדִיפָה — לָא. פְּשִׁיטָא!

a12.he: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: צַעְרֵיהּ הוּא דְּמִדְּכַר, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.

a13.he: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לָא תֵּימָא בִּשְׁעַת רְדִיפָה — אִין, אֲבָל שֶׁלֹּא בִּשְׁעַת רְדִיפָה — לָא, אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ לְאַחַר רְדִיפָה נָמֵי. מַאי טַעְמָא? צַעֲרֵיהּ [הוּא] דְּמִדְּכַר.

a14.he: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: מוּתָּר לְהַטִּיל מוּם בִּבְכוֹר קוֹדֶם שֶׁיָּצָא לַאֲוִיר הָעוֹלָם. אָמַר רָבָא: גַּדְיָא בְּאוּדְנֵיהּ, אִימְּרָא בְּשִׂפְוָותֵיהּ. אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: אִימְּרָא נָמֵי בְּאוּדְנֵיהּ, אֵימוֹר דֶּרֶךְ צְדָעָיו נְפַק.

a15.he: אָמַר רָבָא: אָכֵל וְלָא מִיחֲזֵי, פָּעֵי וּמִיחֲזֵי — הָוֵי מוּמָא. מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן? תְּנֵינָא: הַחוּטִין הַחִיצוֹנוֹת — שֶׁנִּפְגְּמוּ וְשֶׁנִּגְמְמוּ, הַפְּנִימִיּוֹת — שֶׁנֶּעֶקְרוּ. מַאי טַעְמָא? לָאו מִשּׁוּם דְּכִי פָּעֵי מִיחְזֵי?!

a16.he: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: רָבָא נָמֵי טַעְמָא דְמַתְנִיתִין מְפָרֵשׁ, מַאי טַעְמָא נֶעְקְרוּ הָוֵי מוּמָא — מִשּׁוּם דְּכִי פָּעֵי מִיחְזֵי.

a17.he: מַתְנִי׳ כׇּל הַמּוּמִין הָרְאוּיִין לָבֹא בִּידֵי אָדָם, רוֹעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל נֶאֱמָנִין, רוֹעִים כֹּהֲנִים אֵינָן נֶאֱמָנִין. רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: נֶאֱמָן הוּא עַל שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ, וְאֵין נֶאֱמָן עַל שֶׁל עַצְמוֹ. רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: הֶחָשׁוּד עַל הַדָּבָר, לֹא דָּנוֹ וְלֹא מְעִידוֹ.

a18.he: גְּמָ׳ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, חַד אָמַר: ״רוֹעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל״ בֵּי כֹהֲנִים — נֶאֱמָנִין, לִלְגִימָא לָא חָיְישִׁינַן.

a19.he: רוֹעֵי כֹּהֲנִים בֵּי יִשְׂרָאֵל — אֵין נֶאֱמָנִין, מֵימָר אָמַר: כֵּיוָן דְּקָא טָרַחְנָא בֵּיהּ, לָא שָׁבֵיק לְדִידִי וְיָהֵיב לְאַחֲרִינֵי.

a20.he: וְהוּא הַדִּין כֹּהֵן לְכֹהֵן, דְּחָיְישִׁינַן לְגוֹמְלִין.

a21.he: וַאֲתָא רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לְמֵימַר: נֶאֱמָן הוּא עַל שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ, וְאֵינוֹ נֶאֱמָן עַל שֶׁל עַצְמוֹ. וַאֲתָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר לְמֵימַר: הֶחָשׁוּד עַל הַדָּבָר לֹא דָּנוֹ וְלֹא מְעִידוֹ.

a22.he: וְחַד אָמַר: ״רוֹעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל״ וְהֵן כֹּהֲנִים — נֶאֱמָנִין,

b1.he: מֵימָר אָמַר: לָא שָׁבֵיק צוּרְבָּא מֵרַבָּנַן וְיָהֵיב לְדִידִי. ״רוֹעֵי כֹהֲנִים״ וְהֵן יִשְׂרָאֵל — אֵינָן נֶאֱמָנִין, דְּחָיְישִׁינַן לִלְגִימָא.

b2.he: וְכׇל שֶׁכֵּן כֹּהֵן לְכֹהֵן, דְּחָיְישִׁינַן לְגוֹמְלִין, וְחָיְישִׁינַן לִלְגִימָא. וַאֲתָא רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן לְמֵימַר: נֶאֱמָן עַל שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ, וְאֵינוֹ נֶאֱמָן עַל שֶׁל עַצְמוֹ. וַאֲתָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר לְמֵימַר: הֶחָשׁוּד עַל הַדָּבָר, לֹא דָּנוֹ וְלֹא מְעִידוֹ.

b3.he: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר: רוֹעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְהֵן כֹּהֲנִים נֶאֱמָנִין — הַיְינוּ דַּאֲתָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר לְמֵימַר: הֶחָשׁוּד עַל הַדָּבָר לֹא דָּנוֹ וְלֹא מְעִידוֹ.

b4.he: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר: רוֹעֵי כֹהֲנִים בֵּי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֵין נֶאֱמָנִין — מַאי אֲתָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר לְאַשְׁמוֹעִינַן? הַיְינוּ תַּנָּא קַמָּא!

b5.he: אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קַפּוֹסַאי, דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קַפּוֹסַאי אוֹמֵר: בְּכוֹר בֵּי כֹהֵן צָרִיךְ שְׁנַיִם מִן הַשּׁוּק לְהָעִיד עָלָיו.

b6.he: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ בְּנוֹ, אֲפִילּוּ בִּתּוֹ. רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ עֲשָׂרָה וְהֵן בְּנֵי בֵיתוֹ אֵין מְעִידִין עָלָיו.

b7.he: כְּמַאן אָזְלָא הָא דְּאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר רַב קַטִּינָא: סְפֵק בְּכוֹר שֶׁנּוֹלַד בֵּי יִשְׂרָאֵל, צָרִיךְ שְׁנַיִם מִן הַשּׁוּק לְהָעִיד עָלָיו?

b9.he: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: בְּעָלִים מְעִידִין עָלָיו, דְּאִי לָא תֵּימָא הָכִי, מַעֲשֵׂר לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר מִי מֵעִיד עָלָיו?

b10.he: מַעֲשֵׂר וַדַּאי מְהֵימַן, דְּאִי בָּעֵי שָׁדֵי בֵּיהּ מוּמָא בְּכוּלֵּיהּ עֶדְרֵיהּ. אֶלָּא סְפֵק בְּכוֹר, לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר מִי מֵעִיד עָלָיו?

b11.he: וְכִי תֵּימָא, הָכִי נָמֵי דְּלֵית לֵיהּ תַּקַּנְתָּא, וְהָתְנַן, שֶׁהָיָה רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: כֹּל שֶׁחֲלִיפָיו בְּיַד כֹּהֵן פָּטוּר מִן הַמַּתָּנוֹת, וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר מְחַיֵּיב!

b12.he: אֶלָּא שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: בְּעָלִים מְעִידִין עָלָיו, כֹּהֲנִים הוּא דַּחֲשִׁידִי אַמּוּמֵי, יִשְׂרָאֵל לָא חֲשִׁידִי אַמּוּמֵי.

b13.he: אִיתְּמַר: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, רָבָא אָמַר: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי.

b14.he: וּמִי אָמַר רָבָא הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רָבָא: בְּעָלִים עוֹמְדִים עִמָּנוּ בַּחוּץ, נִכְנַס שָׁלֵם וְיָצָא חָבוּל — מְעִידִין עָלָיו! אֵימָא: כׇּל בְּעָלִים עוֹמְדִים, וְלָא חָיְישִׁינַן.

b15.he: אִי הָכִי מַאי לְמֵימְרָא? מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: נֵיחוּשׁ לַחֲשָׁדָא, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן. וְהִלְכְתָא כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, וְדַוְקָא בְּנוֹ וּבִתּוֹ, אֲבָל אִשְׁתּוֹ לָא. מַאי טַעְמָא? אִשְׁתּוֹ כְּגוּפוֹ דָּמֵי.

b16.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי: לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר דְּאָמַר הֶחָשׁוּד עַל הַדָּבָר לֹא דָּנוֹ וְלֹא מְעִידוֹ, וְקָאָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר הֶחָשׁוּד לְדָבָר אֶחָד חָשׁוּד לְכׇל הַתּוֹרָה כּוּלָּהּ, כֹּהֲנִים הָכִי נָמֵי דְּלָא דָּיְינִי דִּינָא? וְהָכְתִיב ״וְעַל פִּיהֶם יִהְיֶה כׇּל רִיב וְכׇל נָגַע״!

messages.text: Continued from 34b: Rabbi Yirmeya asked whether the penalty on one who slits a firstborn’s ear passes to his son after his death. Rabbi Zeira cited Rav Asi’s tradition that a son may sow a field his father improved in the Sabbatical Year, and Abaye now cites another tradition.
that if one rendered impure the ritually pure items of another and died before paying, the Sages did not penalize his son after his death and require him to pay for the damage.

notes.dh: טימא טהרותיו של חבירו ומת לא קנסו בנו אחריו
notes.he: לשלם אע"ג דלדידיה קנסו כדאמרי' בפ' ארבעה אבות נזיקין (ב"ק ד:):
notes.en: If one rendered another’s pure items impure and died, they did not penalize his son after him: to pay, even though they did penalize him himself, as we say in the chapter Arba’a Avot Nezikin (Bava Kamma 4b).

notes.he: טימא טהרותיו לא קנסו בנו לעולם:
notes.en: If one rendered his [fellow’s] pure items impure: they never penalized his son.

messages.text: What is the reason for this? The reason is that damage that is not evident, i.e., which does not involve any visible change, is not considered damage by Torah law. There is a penalty imposed by rabbinic law, as the injured party suffered a loss, but the Sages penalized only him; the Sages did not penalize his son.

notes.he: שהרי טהרות מונחות לפניו ואין היזק ניכר בהן:
notes.en: That is not evident: for the pure items lie before him, and no damage is evident in them.

notes.he: לחיוביה אפי' לדידיה מדאורייתא:
notes.en: Is not considered damage: so as to make him liable by Torah law, even himself.

messages.text: Mishna

There was an incident involving an old ram whose hair was long and dangling, because it was a firstborn offering. And one Roman quaestor [kastor] saw it and said to its owner: What is the status [tivo] of this animal that you allowed it to grow old and you did not slaughter it?

notes.he: לפי שלא היה נגזז מעולם:
notes.en: Mishna. And its hair dangling: because it had never been shorn.

notes.he: ממונה:
notes.en: Kastor: an official.

notes.he: שהניחוהו להזקין כל כך:
notes.en: What is the status of this: that they let it grow so old.

notes.he: שלא היה בו מום ושערו מדולדל לפי שהיה אסור בגיזה:
notes.en: [A gloss notes that the text should read:] “an old male of the ewes,” that is, a firstborn that had no blemish. And its hair dangling, etc.: old, having no blemish, and its hair dangling because it was forbidden to be shorn.

notes.he: היינו בכור):
notes.en: (A male of the ewes: that is, a firstborn.)

messages.text: They said to him: It is a firstborn offering, and therefore it may be slaughtered only if it has a blemish. The quaestor took a dagger [pigom] and slit its ear.

notes.he: רומח:
notes.en: Pigom: a spear.

notes.he: רומח:
notes.en: Pigom: a spear.

messages.text: And the incident came before the Sages for a ruling, and they deemed its slaughter permitted. And after the Sages deemed its slaughter permitted, the quaestor went and slit the ears of other firstborn offerings, but in these cases the Sages deemed their slaughter prohibited, despite the fact that they were now blemished.

notes.he: שהרי אין לומר שהעובד כוכבים הזה להתירו נתכוין שהרי אינו יודע שע"י מום שיעשה בו ישחט אלא א"כ נפל מאליו:
notes.en: And they permitted it: for one cannot say that this gentile intended to make it permitted, since he does not know that it would be slaughtered on account of a blemish that he makes in it, [he knows only that it is slaughtered] if one befalls it by itself.

messages.text: One time children were playing in the field and they tied the tails of lambs to each other, and the tail of one of them was severed, and it was a firstborn offering. And the incident came before the Sages for a ruling and they deemed its slaughter permitted. The people who saw that they deemed its slaughter permitted went and tied the tails of other firstborn offerings, and the Sages deemed their slaughter prohibited.
This is the principle: With regard to any blemish that is caused intentionally, the animal’s slaughter is prohibited; if the blemish is caused unintentionally, the animal’s slaughter is permitted.

notes.he: שלהטיל מום נתכוין להתירו:
notes.en: Any that is intentional: where he intended to inflict a blemish in order to make it permitted.

notes.he: לדעת הבעלים אסור ושלא לדעתו דלא ציוו בפירוש הבעלים לא לקסדור ולא לתינוקות משום הכי התירו. אבל כשצרם באזני בכורות אחרים והתינוקות נמי ולא מיחו בידם הבעלים היינו לדעתם משום הכי אסרו:
notes.en: Any that is with his intent: with the owners’ intent, it is prohibited. And not with his intent: since the owners did not explicitly instruct either the quaestor or the children, therefore they permitted it. But when he slit the ears of other firstborns, and the children too [tied others], and the owners did not stop them, that counts as with their intent; therefore they prohibited them.

messages.text: Gemara

And although the first clause of the mishna mentions a similar occurrence, the incident involving the children is necessary. As, had the tanna taught us only the incident involving the gentile, it might have been thought that the Sages permitted the slaughter of the firstborn offering only there, as it is not a problem if the gentile will acquire the habit of causing blemishes, because that prohibition does not apply to gentiles.
messages.quote: One time children were playing in the field

notes.he: דהתירו בכור ראשון על ידו משום דליכא למימר אתי האי עובד כוכבים למיסרך ללמד להטיל מום בקדשים דסירכיה דעובד כוכבים לא איכפת לן שהרי נהוג הוא באיסורא:
notes.en: Gemara. For had it taught us only the gentile: that they permitted the first firstborn [blemished] through him, because one cannot say this gentile will come to acquire the habit of inflicting blemishes on consecrated animals. A gentile’s habit does not concern us, for he is accustomed to what is prohibited anyway.

notes.he: דקתני והתירו והתירו תרי זמני דאי אשמעינן עובד כוכבים קסדור משום הכי התירו. דלא קא אתי למסרך דלית ביה למיגזר משום מסרך מילתא דעובד כוכבים הוא ולא איכפת (ליה) [לן] באיסור משום הכי התירו:
notes.en: And it is necessary: that it teaches “and they permitted it” twice. For had it taught us only the gentile quaestor, [one would say] that is why they permitted it, since he will not come to acquire the habit: there is no reason to decree on account of habituation, since it is a gentile’s matter and his prohibitions do not concern us; therefore they permitted it.

messages.text: But with regard to a Jewish minor, it is a concern that he is likely to acquire the habit of causing blemishes in firstborn offerings, and therefore one might say that even the first, unintentional time should not be permitted.

notes.he: דאי שרית השתא דילמא אתי למעבד כשהוא גדול אימא לא:
notes.en: But a minor, who will come to acquire the habit: for if you permit it now, perhaps he will come to do it when he is an adult; say [it is] not [permitted].

messages.text: And had the tanna taught us only the incident involving a minor, it might have been thought that the Sages deemed the firstborn offering permitted only there, since there is no concern that people will come to confuse a minor with an adult. People would not erroneously conclude that it is permitted to cause a blemish on a firstborn offering intentionally merely due to an incident involving a minor.

notes.he: דמאן דחזי דהתירו חכמים במום הבא לו ע"י תינוקות לא אתי למימר אי שדי גדול מומא מישתרי דגדול בקטן לא מיחלף:
notes.en: And will not come to confuse with an adult: one who sees that the Sages permitted on account of a blemish that came through children will not come to say that if an adult inflicts a blemish it is permitted, for an adult is not confused with a minor.

notes.he: מעשה דתינוקות משום הכי התירו דלא אתי לאיחלופי בגדול:
notes.en: And had it taught us a minor: the incident of the children, [one would say] that is why they permitted it, since it will not come to be confused with an adult.

messages.text: But in the case of a gentile adult, where this is a concern that people would come to confuse him with a Jewish adult, one might say that even the first, unintentional time should not be permitted. It is therefore necessary for the mishna to teach both cases.

notes.he: אבל עובד כוכבים קסדור דאתי לאיחלופי בגדול ישראל דמאן דחזא לעובד כוכבים גדול דהטיל מום וקסבר דישראל הוא ואתי לאיחלופי בגדול ישראל שמא יטיל מום אימא לא לישרו צריכא:
notes.en: But a gentile quaestor, who will come to be confused with an adult Israelite: for one who sees an adult gentile inflict a blemish and thinks he is a Jew would come to confuse him with an adult Jew [and think] that he may inflict a blemish. Say they should not permit it; [therefore] it is necessary.

messages.text: They taught that the firstborn offering is permitted only in a case where the bystanders said to the quaestor: A firstborn offering may not be slaughtered unless it has a blemish, as this is referring to a blemish that develops naturally.
messages.quote: it may be slaughtered only if it has a blemish

notes.he: דמותר הבכור ע"י העובד כוכבים:
notes.en: They taught only: that the firstborn is permitted through the gentile.

notes.he: לקסדור אינו נשחט אלא א"כ היה בו מום דמשמע שיפול בו מום ממילא דליכא למימר דמדבריהם למד עובד כוכבים דניחא להו שיפיל בו מום:
notes.en: Only where they said to him: to the quaestor, “It is not slaughtered unless it had a blemish,” which implies that a blemish will befall it by itself. So one cannot say that the gentile learned from their words that they would like him to inflict a blemish on it.

notes.he: לא שנו דהתירו אלא דאמרי ליה לקסדור אינו נשחט אלא א"כ היה בו מום אבל אמר כו':
notes.en: They taught that they permitted it only where they said to the quaestor, “It is not slaughtered unless it had a blemish,” but if he said, etc.

messages.text: But if they said to him that a firstborn offering may be slaughtered only if a blemish was caused to form upon it, which indicates human intervention, it is considered as though they explicitly told him: Go and cause a blemish on it, in which case the animal is prohibited.

notes.he: משמע ע"י אדם:
notes.en: Was caused: implies through a person.

messages.text: Now consider, both expressions in fact indicate that the blemish occurred by itself, as both statements are in the passive. Accordingly, what difference is it to me whether the bystanders used the expression: If it had a blemish, or the expression: A blemish was caused in it? Rather, the expression: Was caused, also indicates that it occurred by itself, and there is no difference between the expressions. In both instances the firstborn offering would be permitted.

notes.he: שלא היה יודע העובד כוכבים שיהא מותר על ידו ולא להתיר נתכוין:
notes.en: It is by itself: for the gentile did not know that it would become permitted through him, and he did not intend to make it permitted.

messages.text: What does this principle serve to add? It serves to add an indirect action, i.e., a blemish caused in this manner is also considered an intentional act and the animal may not be slaughtered on its account.
messages.lead: The mishna teaches that this is the principle: In the case of any blemish that is caused with his intent, the animal’s slaughter is prohibited.

notes.he: אם הניח בצק ודבילה ע"ג אוזן הבכור כדי שיבא הכלב ויטלנו:
notes.en: An indirect action: if he placed dough or a pressed fig on the firstborn’s ear so that a dog would come and take it.

notes.he: שמניח בצק או דבילה באזנו:
notes.en: To add an indirect action: that he places dough or a pressed fig on its ear.

messages.text: What is added by the phrase in the second part of the principle: If the blemish was caused without his intent, the animal’s slaughter is permitted? This serves to add an instance where a gentile did not inquire about the nature of the firstborn offering, but rather discovered it from one who speaks offhandedly. Although the gentile intentionally caused a blemish in the animal, since the Jew did not intentionally prompt him to cause it, the animal is permitted.
messages.quote: if the blemish is caused unintentionally, the animal’s slaughter is permitted

notes.he: שלא שאלם קסדור מה טיבו אלא הם עצמן מסיחין לפי תומם ואומרים ראה לא ישחט זה לעולם אלא ע"י מום ולא נתכוונו לכך שיטיל בו מום:
notes.en: Speaks offhandedly: the quaestor did not ask them what its status was; rather they themselves spoke offhandedly and said, “See, this one will never be slaughtered except through a blemish,” and they did not intend that he inflict a blemish on it.

notes.he: לאיתויי מסיח לפי תומו דאפי' דאמר אא"כ נעשה בו מום קרי מסיח לפי תומו:
notes.en: To add one who speaks offhandedly: for even if he said “unless a blemish was caused in it,” it is called speaking offhandedly.

messages.text: Mishna
If one’s firstborn offering was pursuing him, and he kicked the animal and caused a blemish in it, he may slaughter the animal on account of that blemish.

notes.he: איל מנגח רודפו לאדם לנגחו ובעטו אדם לבכור ועשה בו מום:
notes.en: Mishna. If a firstborn was [pursuing him]: a goring ram pursuing a person to gore him, and the person kicked the firstborn and made a blemish in it.

notes.he: ואפי' כהן לפי שלהצלתו נתכוין:
notes.en: He may slaughter on its account: even a priest, since he intended to save himself.

notes.he: איל רודפו לנגחו ובעטו הנרדף כדי להבריחו ממנו ועשה בו מום הרי זה ישחט עליו דלא נתכוון לעשות בו מום:
notes.en: If a firstborn was [pursuing him]: a ram pursuing him to gore him, and the one pursued kicked it to drive it away from him and made a blemish in it: he may slaughter it on its account, since he did not intend to make a blemish in it.

messages.text: Gemara

They taught that the firstborn offering may be slaughtered only in an instance where he kicked it at the time of its pursuit. But if the individual kicked the animal after its pursuit, it may not be slaughtered, as he intended to cause a blemish in order to render it permitted to be slaughtered.
messages.quote: he kicked the animal and caused a blemish in it

messages.text: It is obvious that it is not permitted to slaughter the animal in such a case.

Rav Pappa’s statement is necessary, lest you say that it is in fact permitted to slaughter the firstborn offering since he kicked it after its pursuit only out of anger, as he recalls his distress caused by its pursuit of him, and not in order to render the animal permitted to be slaughtered. Rav Pappa therefore teaches us that it is assumed that he kicked the animal with the express intention of causing a blemish in it, not merely out of anger, and therefore it may not be slaughtered.

notes.he: מה שרדפו:
notes.en: Gemara. His distress: that it pursued him.

notes.he: מה שנגחו ומחמת כן הוא בועטו ואינו מתכוין למום ולישרי קמ"ל דלא:
notes.en: He recalls his distress: that it gored him, and on account of that he kicks it and does not intend [to cause] a blemish, so let it be permitted; it teaches us [that it is] not.

messages.text: Do not say that if the individual kicked the firstborn offering at the time of the pursuit, then yes, it is permitted to slaughter it, but if he kicked it not at the time of the pursuit, it is not permitted to slaughter it. Rather, even if he kicked it after its pursuit of him, it is also permitted. What is the reason? It is assumed that he kicked it after the pursuit not with the intention of causing a blemish, but because he recalls his distress caused by its pursuit of him.
messages.lead: There are those who say the opposite version of this discussion:

messages.text: § It is permitted to cause a blemish in a firstborn fetus before it emerges into the air of the world, as it obtains its sacred status only when it is born.

notes.he: דבכור אינו קדוש עד שתקדשו רחם:
notes.en: Before it emerges into the air of the world: for a firstborn is not sacred until the womb sanctifies it.

notes.dh: מותר לאדם להטיל מום בבכור קודם שיצא כולו לאויר העולם
notes.he: כי היכי דלא ליתו ביה לידי תקלה. אבל אחר שיצא כולו אסור. דהא קידשוהו כותלי רחם:
notes.en: A person is permitted to inflict a blemish on a firstborn before it has entirely emerged into the air of the world: so that they not come to a stumbling block through it. But after it has entirely emerged it is prohibited, for the walls of the womb have sanctified it.

messages.text: In the case of a kid, it is practical to cause a blemish on its ear. Since a kid’s ears are long they emerge from the birth canal prior to the head. With regard to a lamb, whose ears are short and do not appear before the head, it is practical to cause a blemish only on its lip.

notes.he: גדי אזניו ארוכות וקודם שיצא כל ראשו נראין אזניו ויכול להטיל מום דכל זמן שלא יצא כל ראשו אינו כילוד:
notes.en: A kid, on its ear: a kid’s ears are long, and before its whole head emerges its ears are visible, and he can inflict a blemish; for as long as its whole head has not emerged it is not considered born.

notes.he: ששפתיו נראין תחלה ואזניו קשורות ואינן נראות עד שיצא כל ראשו:
notes.en: A lamb, on its lip: for its lips are visible first, while its ears are bound [against its head] and are not visible until its whole head has emerged.

notes.he: כשרואה שמיעוט הראש בחוץ יכול להטיל מום באוזן ואין לו לחוש מרישא האוזן שמא יצא רוב הראש וחזר דמתוך שאזני הגדי גדולות דרך אזנים לצאת במיעוט הראש אימרא בשפוותיה אבל באזניה לא ויש לו לחוש שמא יצא רוב הראש וחזר:
notes.en: A kid, on its ear: when he sees that a minority of the head is outside, he may inflict a blemish on the ear, and from [seeing] the tip of the ear he need not be concerned that perhaps most of the head emerged and went back in; since a kid’s ears are large, the ears normally come out with a minority of the head. A lamb, on its lips, but not on its ears: [there] he must be concerned that perhaps most of the head emerged and went back in.

notes.he: לפי שהגדי אזניו גדולות ומוציאן חוץ לרחם קודם שאר אבריו ויכול להטיל בהן מום וכן אימרא מוציא שפתיו קודם:
notes.en: On its ear: because a kid’s ears are large and it brings them out of the womb before its other limbs, and he can inflict a blemish on them; and likewise a lamb brings its lips out first.

messages.text: In the case of a lamb as well, it is practical to cause a blemish on its ear, as one can say that it emerges from the birth canal through its temples, in which case its ears are visible first.
messages.lead: There are those who say that there is a different version of this statement:

notes.he: טונפל"ש:
notes.en: Its temples: (Rashi adds an Old French gloss).

notes.dh: איכא דאמרי אימרא נמי באודניה [אימור] דרך צדעין נפק
notes.he: כיון שרואה עכשיו מיעוט אוזן אין לומר שמא יצא ראשו ורובו וחזר והא אימר כמו ודאי כמו חיישי' שמא חוץ לחומה לנו דפרק השואל בשבת (דף קנא.) ודחיישינן שמא איחרוהו וכתבוהו דפרק אחד דיני ממונות (סנהדרין לב.) ורבא דהכא ס"ל כרב חסדא דפ' בהמה המקשה (חולין סט:) דלרב הונא דאמר התם יצא שליש ומכרו לעובד כוכבים ויצא שליש אחר קדוש ולא חלה המכירה כלל כיון דנפק לבסוף רובא דאיתגלי מילתא דלמפרע קדוש א"כ הכא נמי שיצא רוב אחרי כן איגלאי מילתא דהוה קדוש מעיקרא ונתחייב ממה שמטיל מום בבכור ואיכא לאוקמי הא דרב יהודה אליבא דרב הונא כשלא יצא כלל וסוגיא נמי דריש כיצד מערימין (תמורה כד:) דמוקי דרב יהודה בזמן הזה ולא חזי להקרבה ופריך אי בזמן הזה מאי למימרא ומשני מהו דתימא נגזר דילמא נפיק רוב ראשו וקא שדי מומא קמ"ל ההיא נמי דלא כרב הונא דלדידיה במיעוט ראשו נמי איכא איסורא ולא ה"ל למינקט רוב ראשו ועוד התם דקאמר ליה רב עמרם לרב ששת אמר על הבכור עם יציאת רובו יהא עולה עולה הוי או בכור הוי נמי דלא כרב הונא דמשמע דפשיטא דקודם יציאת רובו יכול להפקיע קדושת בכור אם לא נחלק בין מכירה להנך:
notes.en: In brief: “There are those who say a lamb also on its ear; say it emerges through its temples”: since he now sees a minority of the ear, one does not say that perhaps its head, or most of it, emerged and went back in; and this “say” is like a certainty, as in “we are concerned that perhaps they lodged outside the wall” (Shabbat 151a) and “we are concerned that perhaps they postponed it and wrote it” (Sanhedrin 32a). Rava here holds like Rav Ḥisda (Ḥullin 69b). For according to Rav Huna there, who says that if a third emerged and he sold it to a gentile and then another third emerged, it is sacred and the sale did not take effect, since once the majority emerged it was revealed retroactively that it was sacred, here too, once the majority emerges afterward, it would be revealed that it was sacred from the start, and he would be liable for blemishing a firstborn. Rav Yehuda’s statement can be set according to Rav Huna where it had not emerged at all. The passage in Temura 24b, which sets Rav Yehuda’s statement in the present time and says “lest you say we should decree lest most of its head emerge,” is also not according to Rav Huna, for whom even a minority of the head would be prohibited. So too Rav Amram’s question to Rav Sheshet there (“with the emergence of most of it let it be a burnt offering”) implies that before most of it emerges one can annul its firstborn sanctity, which is not according to Rav Huna, unless we distinguish between a sale and those cases. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

notes.he: והוציא צדעיו ואזניו קודם שאר אבריו:
notes.en: A lamb emerges through its temples: it brought out its temples and ears before its other limbs.

messages.text: In a case where a firstborn has a blemish in its mouth, if, when it eats, the blemish is not visible, but when it opens its mouth wide and cries out, it is visible, this is considered a blemish, rendering the animal fit for slaughter.

notes.he: אם לבכור יש לו מום בתוך פיו וכי אכיל לא מיחזי אפילו הכי כי פעי מיחזי הוי מום שבגלוי ונשחט עליו דאמרי' בפירקין דלקמן (בכורות דף לז.) דאינו נשחט אלא על מום שבגלוי:
notes.en: It eats and it is not visible: if the firstborn has a blemish inside its mouth, and when it eats it is not visible, nevertheless, since when it cries out it is visible, it is an exposed blemish and it is slaughtered on its account. For we say in the coming chapter (Bekhorot 37a) that it is slaughtered only for an exposed blemish.

notes.he: צועק ופותח פיו הרבה:
notes.en: Pa’ei: it cries out and opens its mouth wide.

notes.he: אי צרם שפתיו וכשהוא אכיל לא מיתחזא במומא וכשהוא פעי מיתחזי:
notes.en: If he slit its lips, and when it eats it does not appear as a blemish, but when it cries out it is visible.

messages.text: What is this teaching us? We learn this in the mishna (39a) with regard to blemishes that render a firstborn offering fit for slaughter:
messages.quote: when it cries out, it is visible

messages.text: The external gums that were damaged and lacking or that were scratched, and likewise, the internal gums that were entirely extracted, are considered blemished.

notes.he: ככי דשיני שקורין ינציב"ה. החיצונות אותם שלפנים כנגד חוטמו שניטל שנפגמו מהם מעט:
notes.en: The external ḥutin: the gums of the teeth, (Rashi adds an Old French gloss). The external ones are those in front, opposite its nose, which were damaged, with a little missing from them.

notes.he: שנחתכו ברחבן מלמעלה בעומק ולא חיסרו כלום הוי מום הואיל ונראו אותן חוטין:
notes.en: Or that were scratched: cut across their width from above, in depth, without anything missing. It is a blemish, since those gums are visible.

notes.he: שהשיניים הגדולות קבועות בהן שקורין מיישיליר"ש:
notes.en: The internal ones: in which the large teeth are set, (Rashi adds an Old French gloss).

notes.he: לגמרי הוי מום כדמפרש ואזיל הואיל וכי פעי מיחזי אבל פגימה או גימום אינו ניכר בהם שהרי חבואות בפה:
notes.en: That were extracted: entirely, it is a blemish, as he goes on to explain, since when it cries out it is visible. But damage or scratching is not noticeable in them, for they are hidden in the mouth.

notes.he: השינים החיצונות שעומדות לפני הפה:
notes.en: The ḥutin: the outer teeth that stand at the front of the mouth.

notes.he: שנחתכו והעיקרין קיימין:
notes.en: And when they were scratched: that were cut, while the roots remain.

notes.he: שינים שנעקרו לגמרי הוי מום:
notes.en: And the internal: teeth that were entirely uprooted; it is a blemish.

messages.text: What is the reason that if the internal gums were extracted it is considered a blemish? Is it not because when the animal opens its mouth wide and cries out, it is visible? If so, what is the novelty of Rava’s statement?

Rava is not in fact teaching a novel halakha. Rather, he is explaining the reason for the ruling of the mishna: What is the reason that if the internal gums were extracted it is considered a blemish? It is that when the animal opens its mouth wide and cries out, the blemish is visible.

notes.he: הוי פנימיות מום אפילו בעיקרה:
notes.en: What is the reason: that the internal ones are a blemish, even [only] when uprooted.

messages.text: Mishna

With regard to all the blemishes that are capable of being brought about by a person, Israelite shepherds are deemed credible to testify that the blemishes were not caused intentionally. But priest-shepherds are not deemed credible, as they are the beneficiaries if the firstborn is blemished.

notes.he: שיש לומר אדם הטילו בו כגון נסמית עינו נקטעה ידו נסדקה אזנו:
notes.en: Mishna. That are capable of being brought about by a person: where one can say a person inflicted it, for example its eye was blinded, its foreleg was cut off, its ear was slit.

notes.he: לומר מאליהן נארעו לו:
notes.en: Israelite shepherds are deemed credible: to say that they befell it by themselves.

notes.he: דנחשדו בדבר. ובגמרא מפרש מאי קרי רועי ישראל ומאי קרי רועי כהנים. האי דנקט ראויין לבא בידי אדם לפי שיש מומין שאין ראויין לבא בידי אדם כגון בעל חמש רגלים או עינו אחת גדולה כשל עגל או קטנה כשל אווז דהוי מום שאין אדם נחשד עליו:
notes.en: Priest-shepherds are not deemed credible: for they are suspect in the matter. The Gemara explains what it calls Israelite shepherds and what it calls priest-shepherds. The reason it specifies “capable of being brought about by a person” is that there are blemishes that cannot come about through a person, such as an animal with five legs, or one whose one eye is large like a calf’s or small like a goose’s, which is a blemish a person is not suspected of [causing].

notes.he: לומר מעצמו נעשה מום זה ומום זה התירו חכם:
notes.en: Israelite shepherds are deemed credible: to say that this blemish came about by itself, and a Sage permitted this blemish.

notes.he: רועים כהנים אין נאמנין דחשודין הן להטיל מומין:
notes.en: Priest-shepherds are not deemed credible: for they are suspect of inflicting blemishes.

messages.text: A priest is deemed credible to testify about the firstborn of another, but is not deemed credible to testify about the firstborn belonging to him.
A priest who is suspect about the matter of causing a blemish may neither adjudicate nor testify in cases involving that matter, even on behalf of another.

notes.he: דרשב"ג ור"מ מפרש בגמ':
notes.en: [The views] of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel and Rabbi Meir are explained in the Gemara.

messages.text: Gemara
Rabbi Yoḥanan and Rabbi Elazar disagree with regard to the meaning of the mishna.

The case of Israelite shepherds is where the shepherds are in the house of priests, i.e., in the employ of a priest. These shepherds are deemed credible to testify that the blemishes were not caused intentionally, as we are not concerned they are lying for a swallow [lilegima] of the firstborn that their priest employer might give them in exchange.

notes.he: מתני' דקתני רועי ישראל נאמנין אפילו הן עומדים בבית הכהנים שהבכור שלהם:
notes.en: Gemara. One says: the mishna, which teaches “Israelite shepherds are deemed credible,” [means] even when they are in the house of priests to whom the firstborn belongs.

notes.he: דליחשדיה שמא על ידי אדם בא לו בכוונה ורועה זה משקר ובא להתירו כדי שישחטו רבו כהן ויאכילנו ממנו עמו:
notes.en: We are not concerned for a swallow: that we should suspect that it came about through a person intentionally and this shepherd is lying, coming to make it permitted so that his master, a priest, will slaughter it and feed him some of it with him.

notes.he: ר"י ור"א מפרשי מתנית' רועי ישראל בי כהנים רועי בהמות כהנים נאמנין לומר מום זה מעצמו היה והתירו חכם:
notes.en: Rabbi Yoḥanan and Rabbi Elazar explain the mishna: “Israelite shepherds” in the house of priests, shepherding priests’ animals, are deemed credible to say this blemish came by itself and a Sage permitted it.

notes.he: כלומר דלא אמרינן דמשום הכי משתרי עילויה דבעו למיכל מיניה בי רביה כהן:
notes.en: We are not concerned for a swallow: that is, we do not say that this is why it is being permitted on his word, because they want to eat of it in the house of his master, the priest.

messages.text: And the case of priest-shepherds is where the shepherds are in the house of an Israelite, i.e., in the latter’s employ. In such a case, the priest-shepherds are not deemed credible to testify that the blemishes were not caused intentionally, as the priest-shepherd can say: Since I have toiled with this firstborn offering, my Israelite employer will not forsake me and give it to another priest. The priest is assumed to be lying, as he has a motive to cause a blemish in the animal.

notes.he: והא דקתני רועי כהנים אין נאמנין הכי קאמר רועים שהן כהנים אין נאמנין אם הבכור ביד ישראל דנחשד האי כהן רועה שהוא עצמו הטילו בו:
notes.en: And that which it teaches, “Priest-shepherds are not deemed credible,” means this: shepherds who are priests are not deemed credible if the firstborn is in an Israelite’s possession, for this priest-shepherd is suspected of having inflicted it himself.

notes.he: לא שביק לדידי ויהיב ליה לכהן אחרינא:
notes.en: For he says: [the Israelite] will not leave me and give it to another priest.

messages.text: And the same is true in the case of a priest who testifies for the sake of another priest. Although the first priest would not derive benefit from his testimony immediately, he is nevertheless not deemed credible to testify, as we are concerned about reciprocal behavior, i.e., the other priest might later repay the favor and lie on his behalf.

notes.he: כלומר ומסברא נפקא לן דכהן רועה אינו נאמן להעיד על הבכור של כהן אחר דחיישינן לגומלין דסבר אעידנו עכשיו והוא יגמול לי כשיתן לי ישראל בכור תם ואטיל בו מום ויבא כהן זה ויעידני שמאליו נפל בו מום:
notes.en: And the same is true of a priest for a priest: that is, we derive by reasoning that a priest-shepherd is not credible to testify about the firstborn of another priest, for we are concerned about reciprocity. He thinks: I will testify for him now, and he will repay me when an Israelite gives me an unblemished firstborn and I inflict a blemish on it; this priest will then come and testify for me that a blemish befell it by itself.

notes.he: כהן לכהן דאין נאמנין דחיישינן לגומלין דשמא זה מתכוין להתיר בכורו כדי שיחזור זה למחר ויעיד על בכורו של זה ויתירו:
notes.en: And the same is true of a priest for a priest: a priest is not credible for a priest, for we are concerned about reciprocity: perhaps this one means to make the other’s firstborn permitted so that the other will in turn testify tomorrow about this one’s firstborn and they will permit it.

messages.text: And Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel comes to say that the testimony of a priest in such a case, when he testifies about the firstborn of another priest, is deemed credible, as there is no concern about reciprocal behavior. But he is not deemed credible with regard to his own firstborn.

notes.he: בין רבו בין אחר דלא נחשדו כהנים אלא על הבכור עצמו שכבר נתנו לו ישראל:
notes.en: About that of another: whether his master or someone else, for priests were suspected only about the firstborn itself that an Israelite has already given him.

notes.he: ואתא רבן [שמעון בן] גמליאל למימר נאמן הוא על של חברו דלא חייש לגומלין:
notes.en: And Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel comes to say: he is credible about another’s, for he is not concerned about reciprocity.

messages.text: And Rabbi Meir comes to say that a priest, who is suspect about the matter of causing a blemish, may neither adjudicate nor testify in cases involving that matter, even on behalf of another. The difference between the opinion of Rabbi Meir and that of the first tanna will be discussed further on.

notes.he: דהיינו כהנים שנחשדו על הבכורות:
notes.en: Who is suspect about the matter: that is, priests, who were suspected about firstborns.

notes.he: ולקמיה פריך ר"מ היינו ת"ק:
notes.en: May neither adjudicate nor testify: further on the Gemara objects [that on one reading] Rabbi Meir is the same as the first tanna.

messages.text: The case of Israelite shepherds is where the shepherds are priests in the employ of an Israelite. The mishna is teaching that these shepherds are deemed credible to testify that the blemishes on their employer’s firstborn offering were not caused intentionally, as they are not suspected of lying in order to obtain its meat,

notes.he: מתניתין דקתני רועי ישראל נאמנין ה"ק רועי בהמות ישראל אע"פ שהן כהנים הרועין נאמנין דמה לו לשקר:
notes.en: And one says: the mishna that teaches “Israelite shepherds are deemed credible” means this: shepherds of Israelites’ animals, even though the shepherds are priests, are credible, for what reason has he to lie?

notes.dh: וחד אמר רועי ישראל והן כהנים
notes.he: כלומר רועין של ישראל ואותן רועין הוויין כהנים נאמנין:
notes.en: And one says: “Israelite shepherds,” and they are priests; that is, shepherds of Israelites, and those shepherds are priests, are credible.

messages.text: as it is assumed that the priest-shepherd would say: My Israelite employer will not forsake a priest who is a Torah scholar and give the blemished animal to me, an unlearned shepherd.

notes.he: האי ישראל כהן צורבא מרבנן ויהיב לי לדידי דסתם רועה עם הארץ הוא:
notes.en: He says, he will not leave: this Israelite [will not leave] a priest who is a Torah scholar and give it to me, for an ordinary shepherd is an am ha’aretz.

notes.dh: מימר אמר לא שביק צורבא מדרבנן ויהיב לדידי
notes.he: והא דאמר לעיל בסוף פרק ב' (בכורות דף יח:) בחצר בעל הבית ורועה כהן דלר"ט אקנויי מקני ליה מקום בחצירו ואפילו ר"ע לא פליג אלא משום דאית [ליה] פסידא לא מקנה [ליה] מידעם התם איירי במכירי כהונה או שאוהבו ורגיל ליתן לו:
notes.en: He says: he will not leave a Torah scholar and give it to me: And as for what is said above at the end of chapter 2 (Bekhorot 18b) about a householder’s courtyard and a priest-shepherd, that according to Rabbi Tarfon he transfers to him a place in his courtyard, and even Rabbi Akiva disagrees only because, since he would have a loss, he does not transfer anything to him [which assumes the owner would give the firstborn to his shepherd]: there it speaks of a priest who is an acquaintance, or whom he loves and regularly gives to.

notes.he: רועה לא שביק צורבא מדרבנן בהו ויהיב ליה לבכור לדידי:
notes.en: For he says: the shepherd [thinks], he will not leave a Torah scholar among them and give the firstborn to me.

messages.text: The case of priest-shepherds is where the shepherds are Israelites in the employ of a priest. These shepherds are not deemed credible to testify, as we are concerned that they might be lying for a swallow of the firstborn that their priest employer would give them in exchange.

notes.he: רועי בהמות של כהנים אע"פ שהרועים ישראל אין נאמנין להעיד על בכורו של רבו כהן דחיישי' ללגימא וכ"ש רועי כהן ובהמות של רבן כהן אין נאמנין דחיישינן לגומלין וללגימא:
notes.en: Priest-shepherds: shepherds of priests’ animals, even though the shepherds are Israelites, are not credible to testify about the firstborn of their master, a priest, for we are concerned for a swallow. And all the more so priest-shepherds with the animals of their master, a priest, are not credible, for we are concerned for reciprocity and for a swallow.

messages.text: And all the more so the testimony of a priest for the sake of another priest is not deemed credible, as we are concerned that the two might engage in reciprocal behavior, and we are concerned that the priest-shepherd might be lying for a swallow of the firstborn offering.

And Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel comes to say that the priest-shepherd is deemed credible to testify with regard to the firstborn offering of another priest, but is not deemed credible to testify with regard to a firstborn belonging to himself. And Rabbi Meir comes to say that a priest who is suspect about the matter of causing a blemish may neither adjudicate nor testify in cases involving that matter, even on behalf of another.

notes.he: אכהן לכהן קאי וקאמר דנאמן הכהן הרועה על של רבו דלא חיישי' לא לגומלין ולא ללגימא:
notes.en: About that of another: this refers to a priest for a priest, and says that the priest-shepherd is credible about his master’s [firstborn], for we are concerned neither for reciprocity nor for a swallow.

notes.he: כהנים חשודים על הבכורות:
notes.en: Who is suspect about the matter: priests, who are suspected about firstborns.

notes.he: ופליג אדר' שמעון דשרי אפי' כהן לכהן ופליג אדתנא קמא דאמר רועי בהמות ישראל ואפילו הן כהנים נאמנין והרועים כהנים אין נאמנין:
notes.en: May neither adjudicate nor testify: he disagrees with Rabbi Shimon [ben Gamliel], who permits even a priest for a priest, and disagrees with the first tanna, who says that shepherds of Israelites’ animals are credible even if they are priests, and that the “priest-shepherds” are not credible.

messages.caption: Who are the mishna’s “Israelite shepherds” and “priest-shepherds”? The two readings of Rabbi Yoḥanan and Rabbi Elazar (the Gemara does not say which is whose).

messages.text: Granted, according to the second opinion, i.e., the one who says the first tanna maintains that the case of Israelite shepherds is where the shepherds are priests in the employ of an Israelite, and they are deemed credible to testify, this is the reason that Rabbi Meir comes to disagree and say that a priest who is suspect about the matter of causing a blemish may neither adjudicate nor testify even for the sake of an Israelite employer.

notes.he: בשלמא למ"ד רועה ישראל והן כהנים נאמנין היינו דקא פליג ר' מאיר עליה:
notes.en: Granted, according to the one who says “Israelite shepherds,” and they are priests, are credible: that is why Rabbi Meir disagrees with him.

messages.text: But according to the first opinion, i.e., the one who says that the first tanna maintains that the case of priest-shepherds is where the shepherds are in an Israelite’s house, and they are not deemed credible to testify, what is Rabbi Meir coming to teach us? This is the same opinion as that of the first tanna himself.

notes.he: דהאמר ת"ק נמי דכהן אינו נאמן:
notes.en: This is the first tanna: for the first tanna also says that a priest is not credible.

notes.he: אלא למ"ד רועי כהנים בי ישראל אין נאמנין ואתא ר' מאיר נמי למימר דאין נאמנין ר' מאיר היינו ת"ק:
notes.en: But according to the one who says priest-shepherds in an Israelite’s house are not credible, and Rabbi Meir also comes to say that they are not credible, Rabbi Meir is the same as the first tanna.

messages.text: There is a difference between the opinions of the first tanna and Rabbi Meir with regard to a statement of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Kefusai. As it is taught in a baraita:

notes.he: איכא בינייהו דר' יהושע בן קפוסאי:
notes.en: There is a difference between them regarding [the statement] of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Kefusai.

notes.dh: איכא בינייהו דרבי יהושע בן קפוסאי
notes.he: דת"ק סבר כוותיה דדווקא רועי כהנים בין בי ישראל בין בי כהנים אינם נאמנים כדאמר טעמא אבל שני כהנים מן השוק נאמנים ולר"מ אפי' שנים מן השוק אין נאמנין דלית ליה כרבי יהושע בן קפוסאי דקסבר ר"מ החשוד על הדבר לא דנו ולא מעידו ושנים מן השוק דקאמר ר' יהושע בן קפוסאי בכהנים איירי דישראל אפילו חד מהימן ולר"מ כל היכא דאסור אפי' שנים אין נאמנין כדאמר בסמוך ספק בכור לר"מ מי מעיד עליו:
notes.en: There is a difference between them regarding Rabbi Yehoshua ben Kefusai: for the first tanna holds like him, that specifically priest-shepherds, whether in an Israelite’s house or in a priest’s house, are not credible, for the reason stated, but two priests from the marketplace are credible; whereas according to Rabbi Meir even two from the marketplace are not credible, for he does not hold like Rabbi Yehoshua ben Kefusai, since Rabbi Meir holds that one who is suspect about the matter may neither adjudicate nor testify. The “two from the marketplace” that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Kefusai speaks of are priests, for an Israelite is credible even alone. And according to Rabbi Meir, wherever it is prohibited even two are not credible, as it says shortly: “An uncertain firstborn, according to Rabbi Meir, who can testify about it?”

notes.he: בין ת"ק ור' מאיר דר' יהושע בן קפוסאי דאמר בכור בי כהן צריך שנים מן השוק להעיד עליו שאותו מום הטיל חכם ואפי' הן כהנים אותן שנים ובלבד שלא יהו מבני ביתו. ת"ק דאמר רועי כהנים בי ישראל אין נאמנין משום דמימר אמר כיון דטרחנא ביה וכו' אבל ב' כהנים מן השוק נאמנין להעיד דהא לא טרחו ביה. ואתא ר' מאיר למימר החשוד על הדבר. כלומר כהנים כיון דחשידי אמומין אפי' ב' מן השוק אי כהנים נינהו אין נאמנין:
notes.en: There is a difference between them, between the first tanna and Rabbi Meir, [regarding the statement] of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Kefusai, who said: a firstborn in a priest’s house requires two from the marketplace to testify about it that a Sage [permitted] that blemish (the printed text reads “inflicted”), even if those two are priests, provided they are not of his household. The first tanna, who said priest-shepherds in an Israelite’s house are not credible because he says “since I toiled with it,” etc., [holds] that two priests from the marketplace are credible to testify, for they did not toil with it. And Rabbi Meir comes to say “one who is suspect about the matter”: that is, since priests are suspected about blemishes, even two from the marketplace, if they are priests, are not credible.

notes.dh: ט"א איכא בינייהו דר' יהושע בן קפוסאי
notes.he: דת"ק לית ליה דר' יהושע אלא ואפילו רועי ישראל בי כהנים נאמן דללגימא לא חיישינן. ואתא ר' מאיר למימר החשוד בדבר כלומר דחשידי אלגימא ואין נאמנין אלא שנים מן השוק:
notes.en: Another version: there is a difference between them [regarding] Rabbi Yehoshua ben Kefusai, for the first tanna does not hold like Rabbi Yehoshua; rather, even Israelite shepherds in priests’ houses are credible, for we are not concerned for a swallow. And Rabbi Meir comes to say “one who is suspect about the matter”: that is, they are suspected regarding a swallow and are not credible; only two from the marketplace [are].

messages.text: If a firstborn animal in the house of a priest developed a blemish, two people from the marketplace, i.e., not from the priest’s household, are required to testify about it that the blemish was not caused deliberately.

notes.he: שנים כל שהן ואפילו כהנים אבל כהנים שבביתו לא. ת"ק אית ליה דרבי יהושע בן קפוסאי דקאמר ת"ק רועי כהנים בין בי ישראל בין בי כהנים כדפרישית טעמא אין נאמנין אבל כהנים דעלמא נאמנין ואפילו אבכורות דכהנים ולא חיישינן לגומלין אלא ברועה דקאי גביה וסבר אעיד את רבי והוא יעידני כשיתן לי ישראל בעלמא בכור ור"מ לית ליה דר' יהושע לגמרי דכיון דנחשדו כהנים על הבכור לא דן ולא מעיד אפילו כהן דשוק ואפי' הבכור ביד ישראל:
notes.en: Requires two from the marketplace: any two, even priests, but not priests of his household. The first tanna holds like Rabbi Yehoshua ben Kefusai, since the first tanna says that priest-shepherds, whether in an Israelite’s house or in a priest’s house, are not credible, for the reason I explained; but ordinary priests are credible, even about priests’ firstborns, and we are concerned about reciprocity only for a shepherd who stands with him, who thinks: I will testify for my master and he will testify for me when some Israelite gives me a firstborn. And Rabbi Meir does not hold like Rabbi Yehoshua at all: since priests were suspected about the firstborn, a priest may neither adjudicate nor testify, even a priest from the marketplace, and even when the firstborn is in an Israelite’s possession.

messages.text: This unqualified statement indicates that the two people can even be priests, provided that they are not household members.
Even the priest’s son and even his daughter may testify about it.

notes.he: ר"ש לטעמיה דאמר נאמן הוא על של חבירו ואביו היינו נמי חבירו דאין כהן נחשד אלא על של עצמו:
notes.en: Even his son and his daughter: Rabbi Shimon [ben Gamliel] follows his own reasoning, for he says a priest is credible about another’s, and [for the son] his father is also “another,” for a priest is suspected only about his own.

messages.text: Even in a case where there are ten people, if they are members of his household, they may not testify about it.

notes.dh: אפי' עשרה והן בני ביתו אין מעידין
notes.he: אבל מן השוק עד אחד נאמן דלר' יהושע צריך שנים מן השוק:
notes.en: Even ten, if they are his household members, may not testify: but from the marketplace one witness is credible, whereas according to Rabbi Yehoshua two from the marketplace are needed.

messages.text: The first tanna of the mishna maintains that only a priest who is a shepherd of the animal in question is not deemed credible to testify, but the testimony of an independent priest is credible. This accords with the opinion of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Kefusai, who allows the testimony of any two independent people, including a priest. Conversely, Rabbi Meir does not deem credible even the testimony of an independent priest, as indicated by his general statement about suspect priests.
In accordance with whose opinion is that which Rav Ḥisda says that Rav Ketina says?
messages.lead: The Gemara discusses a related statement:

messages.text: In the case of an animal whose status as a firstborn is uncertain that was born in the house, i.e., in the possession, of an Israelite, e.g., it was uncertain whether the mother had previously given birth, in which case the animal remains in the possession of the Israelite and may be eaten upon developing a blemish, two people from the marketplace are required to testify about it.

notes.he: דשל ישראל הוא כגון רחלה שלא ביכרה וילדה שני זכרים דאמרי' בפ"ב (לעיל בכורות יז.) אחד לו ואחד לכהן ואת שלו הוי ספק שמא יצא ראשון וירעה עד שיומם ואוכלו ישראל:
notes.en: An uncertain firstborn: that belongs to the Israelite, for example a ewe that had not given birth before and bore two males, of which we say in chapter 2 (above, Bekhorot 17a) that one is his and one is the priest’s. His own is uncertain, perhaps it emerged first; it grazes until it becomes blemished, and the Israelite eats it.

notes.dh: צריך שנים מן השוק להעיד עליו
notes.he: שלא הוטל בו מום בכוונה:
notes.en: Two from the marketplace are required to testify about it: that a blemish was not inflicted on it intentionally.

notes.he: דלאחר שנולד בו מום מצי אכיל ליה ישראל וצריך ב' מן השוק להעיד עליו שהתירו חכם שמותר במומו:
notes.en: An uncertain firstborn in an Israelite’s house: for after it develops a blemish the Israelite may eat it, and two from the marketplace are required to testify about it that a Sage permitted it, that it is permitted with its blemish.

messages.text: In accordance with whose opinion is this statement? It is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Kefusai. Just as he requires two independent people to testify about a firstborn offering in the possession of a priest, as he is suspected of intentionally causing the blemish, so too, he requires two independent people to testify in the case of an uncertain status of a firstborn offering born in the possession of an Israelite.
messages.quote: two people from the marketplace are required to testify about it

notes.he: דכי היכי דבכור בי כהנים בעי שנים מן השוק להעיד עליו ה"נ ספק בכור ביד ישראל:
notes.en: In accordance with Rabbi Yehoshua: for just as a firstborn in a priest’s house requires two from the marketplace to testify about it, so too an uncertain firstborn in an Israelite’s possession.

messages.text: The Israelite owners themselves may testify about it. As, if you do not say so, but instead maintain that any involved person is suspected of deliberately causing a blemish in his firstborn animal, this poses a difficulty with regard to the halakha of an animal tithe offering, which may also be eaten if it developed a blemish. According to Rabbi Meir, who can testify about it?

notes.he: ספק בכור ביד ישראל אפילו בעליו ישראל נאמן דכהנים נחשדו על הבכורות ולא ישראל ואפילו על ספק בכור שנאכל להם:
notes.en: Rav Naḥman says: [regarding] an uncertain firstborn in an Israelite’s possession, even its Israelite owner is credible, for priests were suspected about firstborns, but Israelites were not, even about an uncertain firstborn that is eaten by them.

notes.he: אלא בעלים חשודים עליו אם כן הוי ישראל חשוד על המומין:
notes.en: For if you do not say so: but [say instead] that the owners are suspect about it, then Israelites would be suspect about blemishes.

notes.he: מי מעיד על מומו הא א"ר מאיר החשוד על הדבר לעצמו אינו מעיד לאחרים כדחזינן ר"מ פוסל אפילו כהנים דשוק:
notes.en: Tithe according to Rabbi Meir: who testifies about its blemish? Rabbi Meir has said that one who is suspect about the matter for himself does not testify for others, as we see that Rabbi Meir disqualifies even priests from the marketplace.

notes.he: מעשר בהמה לר' מאיר דאמר החשוד על הדבר לא דנו ולא מעידו נהי דבספק בכור כיון דמילתא דלא שכיחא הוא לא חשידי עליה (כו') ישראל ונאמנין עליו ב' מן השוק אלא מעשר בהמה דשכיח והוא של ישראל שהוא אוכלו כיון דשלו הוא הוי חשוד עליו וכל ישראל חשודין עליו שיש לכל אחד בהמות ויש להן מעשרות:
notes.en: Animal tithe, according to Rabbi Meir, who says one who is suspect about the matter may neither adjudicate nor testify: granted, regarding an uncertain firstborn, since it is an uncommon matter, Israelites are not suspected about it, and two from the marketplace are credible about it. But animal tithe, which is common and belongs to the Israelite, who eats it: since it is his, he is suspect about it, and all Israelites are suspect about it, for every one of them has animals and they have tithes.

messages.text: Rabbi Meir maintains that anyone who is suspect about the matter of causing a blemish on his own behalf may neither adjudicate nor testify in cases involving that matter even on behalf of another. If so, how can anyone, even an Israelite, testify about any blemished animal-tithe offering? It must be that an Israelite is not suspected of deliberately causing blemishes.

With regard to the animal tithe offering, the owner is certainly deemed credible to testify that its blemish occurred naturally, because if he wants, he could legitimately cause a blemish in his entire flock before the obligation to separate tithes came into effect.

notes.he: בתמיה. הא ודאי מהימן אפילו בעליו דהא אי בעי הוי שדי ביה מומא בהיתר בכוליה עדריה קודם שיעשר דאכתי לא קדשא חד מינייהו:
notes.en: Tithe?: said in astonishment. There even its owner is certainly credible, for if he wanted he could have inflicted a blemish permissibly on his entire flock before he tithed, since none of them was yet sanctified.

notes.he: לא דמי דבמעשר ודאי מהימן אפי' בעליו כיון דאיבעי שדי מומא בכוליה עדריה ומגו דלא עבד הכי מהימן:
notes.en: It is not comparable, for regarding tithe he is certainly credible, even its owner, since if he wanted he could cast a blemish on his entire flock; and since he did not do so, he is credible.

messages.text: If an Israelite is not deemed credible to testify about a blemish found on an animal whose status as a firstborn is uncertain, then according to Rabbi Meir, who can testify about it? Both Israelites and priests stand to gain if their animal whose status as a firstborn is uncertain develops a blemish, and therefore no one should be deemed credible to testify about it.
messages.lead: Rather, this is what Rav Naḥman stated:

notes.he: הכי פריך ספק בכור לר"מ אי בעלים חשודים עליה נמצאו ישראל חשודים על ספק בכור וכ"ש כהנים דהא אי הוה נמי בבהמות עדר כהן ספק בכור הנולד בעדרו בעי אמתוני עד שיומם דכהנים לא נפטרו מבכור בהמה טהורה בפרק שני (לעיל בכורות יג.) וא"כ מי מעיד עליו:
notes.en: Rather: this is the objection: an uncertain firstborn according to Rabbi Meir. If the owners are suspect about it, then Israelites are found to be suspect about an uncertain firstborn, and all the more so priests; for even if an uncertain firstborn were born in a priest’s flock it would have to be kept until it became blemished, since priests were not exempted from the firstborn of a kosher animal (chapter 2, above, Bekhorot 13a). If so, who testifies about it?

notes.he: אם בעליו אין מעיד עליו מי מעיד עליו א"ת שנים מן השוק הוי חשידי אספק בכור שלהן והאיך מעידין על זה:
notes.en: Rather, an uncertain firstborn according to Rabbi Meir: if its owner cannot testify about it, who can testify about it? If you say two from the marketplace, they are suspect regarding their own uncertain firstborns, so how can they testify about this one?

messages.text: And if you would say that indeed, according to Rabbi Meir, an animal whose status as a firstborn is uncertain has no remedy that can render it fit for slaughter, as no one is deemed credible to testify about its blemish, this cannot be correct. But didn’t we learn in a mishna (18b) that

notes.he: לר' מאיר:
notes.en: Has no remedy: according to Rabbi Meir.

notes.dh: וכי תימא דלית להו תקנתא כו'
notes.he: הוה מצי למימר דחלקנו בין חבר לעם הארץ כר' יהושע דלקמן וכן בסמוך דפריך כהני ה"נ דלא דייני דינא א"נ ר' יהושע עצמו חוזר בו דקא"ל לר"ג היאך החי יכול להכחיש את החי ופירש שם בקונט' שרוצה לומר ודאי אמרתי וחוזר אני בו ומיהו מסתברא דמשום כבוד דר"ג הוא דקאמר הכי כי ההיא דתפלת ערבית (ברכות דף כז:) שאמר כמו כן אע"פ שלא היה חוזר בו מה שאמר תחלה רשות דהכי פסק רב התם הלכה כדברי האומר רשות:
notes.en: And if you would say they have no remedy, etc.: He could have answered that we distinguish between a ḥaver and an am ha’aretz, like Rabbi Yehoshua further on; and likewise shortly, where it objects “priests too should not adjudicate.” Alternatively, Rabbi Yehoshua himself retracts, for he said to Rabban Gamliel, “How can the living contradict the living?”, and Rashi explains there that he means: I certainly said it, and I retract. However, it is reasonable that he said this out of respect for Rabban Gamliel, as in the case of the evening prayer (Berakhot 27b), where he said the same, though he did not retract his first statement that it is optional; for Rav rules there that the halakha follows the one who says it is optional.

notes.dh: וכי תימא הכי נמי דלית ליה תקנתא
notes.he: דלא מצי הוי חולין דליכא דמהימן לאסהודי עליה:
notes.en: And if you would say that indeed it has no remedy: that it can never become non-sacred, since there is no one credible to testify about it.

messages.text: Rabbi Yosei would say: Any animal whose replacements are in the possession of a priest is exempt from, i.e., not subject to, the mitzva of giving the priestly gifts, and Rabbi Meir deems him obligated to give the gifts.

notes.he: כגון האי ספק בכור שהכהן נטל (את אחיו) פטור ישראל מן המתנות דזרוע ולחיים וקיבה דעשו שאינו זוכה כזוכה כדאמרן בפרק שני (שם יח.) ור"מ מחייב ומדמחייב ליה רבי מאיר במתנות מכלל דבר אכילה הוא:
notes.en: Whose replacements are in the possession of a priest: for example this uncertain firstborn, where the priest took (its brother): [the Israelite] is exempt from the gifts of the foreleg, the jaw and the maw, for they treated one who does not acquire like one who acquires, as we said in chapter 2 (ibid. 18a). And Rabbi Meir deems him obligated; and since Rabbi Meir deems him obligated in the gifts, it follows that it is something that may be eaten.

messages.text: Since Rabbi Meir permits the consumption of an animal whose status as a firstborn is uncertain, evidently he allows testimony about its blemish in such a case.

notes.he: ור' מאיר מחייב במתנות כשהוא נאכל לישראל במומם מכלל דחולין ודאין הן אלא ש"מ דאית ליה תקנתא:
notes.en: But didn’t we learn… and Rabbi Meir deems him obligated in the gifts when it is eaten by an Israelite in its blemished state: this implies that they are certainly non-sacred. Rather, learn from this that it has a remedy.

messages.text: Rather, learn from this that the Israelite owners may testify about their animals whose status as a firstborn are uncertain, despite the fact that priests may not. The reason is that it is only priests who are suspected of causing blemishes; Israelites are not suspected of causing blemishes.

notes.dh: אלא לאו ש"מ בעלים מעידין עליו
notes.he: תימה ורב חסדא דבעי לעיל שנים מן השוק בספק בכור בי ישראל תקשי ליה לר"מ מי מעיד עליו כיון דישראל נמי חשידי וי"ל דהוה משני כדפרישית דחלקנו בין חבר לע"ה א"נ יאמר רב חסדא ספק בכור לא יחמיר ר"מ שלא יהו שנים מן השוק נאמנים:
notes.en: Rather, learn from this that the owners may testify about it: This is puzzling: Rav Ḥisda, who above requires two from the marketplace for an uncertain firstborn in an Israelite’s house, should face the difficulty “according to Rabbi Meir, who can testify about it?”, since Israelites too are suspect. One can say that he would answer as I explained, that we distinguish between a ḥaver and an am ha’aretz. Alternatively, Rav Ḥisda would say that for an uncertain firstborn Rabbi Meir would not be so stringent that two from the marketplace would not be credible.

notes.he: בעליו מעידין עליו משום דישראל לא חשידי אמומי:
notes.en: Its owners may testify about it, because Israelites are not suspected about blemishes.

messages.text: The halakha is in accordance with the opinion of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, that a priest is deemed credible to testify about the blemished firstborn animal of another priest, even if he is a household member.
messages.quote: Even the priest’s son and even his daughter

notes.he: דאפילו בנו ובתו:
notes.en: The halakha follows Rabbi Shimon [ben Gamliel]: that even his son and his daughter [may testify].

notes.he: דאמר אפי' בנו אפי' בתו:
notes.en: The halakha follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, who said even his son, even his daughter.

messages.text: The halakha is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yosei, that one’s household members are not deemed credible to testify.
And does Rava actually say this? But doesn’t Rava say:
messages.quote: in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yosei

messages.text: If the priestly owner of a firstborn animal was standing outside with us, and the animal entered the house whole and emerged injured, the household members may testify about it that the blemish was not caused by a person.

notes.he: של בכור עמנו עומד בחוץ ונכנס הבכור שלם בבית ויצא חבול מעידין עליו אותם שבבית שמאליו נפל בו. אלמא אין נחשד אלא כהן בעל הבית שהבכור שלו כר"ש:
notes.en: The priest, its owner: of the firstborn, is standing outside with us, and the firstborn entered the house whole and emerged injured: those in the house testify about it that [the blemish] befell it by itself. Evidently only the priest, the householder to whom the firstborn belongs, is suspected, in accordance with Rabbi Shimon [ben Gamliel].

notes.he: בעליו של בכור עמנו עומד ונכנס הבכור שלם בתוך ביתו ויצא חבול מעידין עליו בני ביתו שמעצמו היה ונאמנים לומר חכם התירו. אלמא דבני ביתו נאמנין:
notes.en: The owner of the firstborn is standing with us, and the firstborn entered his house whole and emerged injured: his household members testify about it that it happened by itself, and they are credible to say that a Sage permitted it. Evidently his household members are credible.

messages.text: Evidently, Rava maintains that the members of the priest’s household are deemed credible to testify about the priest’s firstborn.

One can say that Rava is referring to a case where all the owners, i.e., the household members, are standing outside, while the shepherd alone remains inside. When the firstborn animal emerges injured, the shepherd is deemed credible to testify about the blemish and we are not concerned that he is lying.

notes.he: בניו ובני ביתו עומדין עמנו בחוץ ומעיד עליו רועה שהיה בבית:
notes.en: Say: all its owners: his sons and household members are standing outside with us, and the shepherd who was in the house testifies about it.

notes.he: אימא כל בעליו עמנו דאפי' ב"ב עמנו דקים לן דאינהו לא הטילו מעידין עליו ב"ב ונאמנין לומר מום זה התיר חכם:
notes.en: Say: all its owners are with us, meaning even the household members are with us, so we know that they did not inflict it; [then] his household members testify about it and are credible to say a Sage permitted this blemish.

messages.text: If so, that all of the household members were outside, what is the purpose of stating that the shepherd is deemed credible? This ruling is obvious.

notes.he: הואיל וכל בעליו עמנו מי יטילנו כו':
notes.en: It is obvious: since all its owners are with us, who would have inflicted it, etc.

notes.he: כיון דכל בעליו עמנו והוי צריכא למימר דמעידין:
notes.en: If so: since all its owners were with us, was it necessary to say that they testify?

messages.text: This ruling is necessary lest you say that we should entertain a suspicion that the shepherd himself caused the blemish. Rava therefore teaches us that this is not so, and the shepherd is deemed credible.

notes.he: דרועה גופיה הטילו בו. ל"א אימא כל בעלים עמנו כלומר אי אמרי סהדי כל בעליו של בכור דהיינו הוא ובני ביתו היו עמנו בחוץ ונכנס הבכור שלם בבית ויצא חבול מעידין כלומר עדותן עדות ושרי הואיל ולא היה איש בבית. ניחוש לחשדא שמא הם גרמו לו מתחלה שהניחו לו דבילה על האזן אי נמי עשו לו גומא ונפל שם:
notes.en: Lest you say we should entertain a suspicion: that the shepherd himself inflicted it. Another explanation: “Say: all its owners are with us,” that is, if witnesses say that all the owners of the firstborn, meaning he and his household, were with us outside, and the firstborn entered the house whole and emerged injured, they may testify, meaning their testimony is valid testimony and it is permitted, since no one was in the house. [Lest you say] we should entertain a suspicion that perhaps they caused it beforehand, by placing a pressed fig on its ear, or by making a pit for it into which it fell.

notes.he: שיחשדו שמא נשאר אחד מן הבית:
notes.en: We should entertain a suspicion: that perhaps one of the household remained [inside].

notes.he: דדילמא הנהו בני ביתיה עבדו להו גרמא מעיקרא ע"י בצק או דבילה או הטילו לו מאכל בין קוצים ולא ליהמנינהו קמ"ל כיון דעמנו היה כל בעליו מעידין עליו ב"ב:
notes.en: Lest you say we should entertain a suspicion: that perhaps those household members set up an indirect cause for it beforehand, with dough or a pressed fig, or threw food for it among thorns, and they should not be believed. It teaches us that since all its owners were with us, his household members testify about it.

messages.text: And the halakha is in accordance with the opinion of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, that a priest’s household members may testify about his blemished firstborn offering. And this applies specifically to his son and daughter, but his wife may not testify. What is the reason? One’s wife is as oneself.

§ @Abaye, according to Rabbi Meir, who says that a priest who is suspect about the matter of causing a blemish may neither adjudicate nor testify in cases involving that matter even on behalf of another, and in addition Rabbi Meir says that one who is suspected of transgressing one matter, i.e., who is known to have committed one transgression, is suspected of transgressing the entire Torah, it should follow that priests should also not be allowed to administer judgment at all. But isn’t it written with regard to the priests: “And according to their word shall every controversy and every stroke be”?

verse.he: וְנִגְּשׁוּ הַכֹּהֲנִים בְּנֵי לֵוִי כִּי בָם בָּחַר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לְשָׁרְתוֹ וּלְבָרֵךְ בְּשֵׁם יְהֹוָה וְעַל־פִּיהֶם יִהְיֶה כׇּל־רִיב וְכׇל־נָגַע׃
verse.en: The priests, sons of Levi, shall come forward; for the ETERNAL your God has chosen them for divine service and to pronounce blessing in the name of GOD, and every lawsuit and case of assault is subject to their ruling.

notes.dh: כהני הכי נמי דלא דייני דינא
notes.he: לרבא דאמר בפ' זה בורר (סנהדרין כז.) אוכל נבילות להכעיס שהוא רע לשמים אינו חשוד להיות רע לבריות לא פריך מידי אבל לאביי התם פריך שפיר ועוד יש לפרש לרבא דמשמע ליה שיש לכהנים להיות כשרים לכל (זמן) דין שבעולם ולכל הוראה כדכתיב (דברים כ״א:ה׳) כל ריב וכל נגע ועוד היה יכול להקשות היאך מותר לאכול משחיטתו והיאך כשרים על כל קרבנות כולם ועוד בלא בכור נמי יכול להקשות לרבי מאיר מטעם דנחשדו כהנים על השביעית כדאמרינן בפרק זה בורר (סנהדרין כו.):
notes.en: Priests, too, should not administer judgment: According to Rava, who says in the chapter Zeh Borer (Sanhedrin 27a) that one who eats unslaughtered carcasses to provoke is wicked toward Heaven but is not suspected of being wicked toward people, this is no objection at all; but according to Abaye there, it is a fine objection. One can further explain [it even] according to Rava: he understands that priests must be fit for every judgment in the world and every ruling, as it is written (Deuteronomy 21:5): “every controversy and every stroke.” He could also have asked: how is it permitted to eat from their slaughtering, and how are they fit for all the offerings? And further, even without the firstborn one could ask this according to Rabbi Meir, because priests were suspected regarding the Sabbatical Year, as we say in the chapter Zeh Borer (Sanhedrin 26a).

messages.text: Continues on 36a with the answer: Rabbi Meir says only that there is a concern priests may have caused a blemish, not that they are established as doing so.
